text: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
author: Will Durant (summarizing Aristotle)

text: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
author: Seneca

text: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
author: Attributed to Seneca

text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

text: No man is free who is not master of himself.
author: Epictetus

text: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
author: Epictetus

text: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
author: Marcus Aurelius (paraphrase)

text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The unexamined life is not worth living.
author: Socrates (Plato, Apology)

text: The beginning is the most important part of the work.
author: Plato

text: Knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom.
author: Attributed to Aristotle

text: Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.
author: Attributed to Aristotle

text: Dripping water hollows out stone, not through force but through persistence.
author: Ovid

text: Fortune favours the bold.
author: Virgil (Aeneid)

text: Perfer et obdura; dolor hic tibi proderit olim. — Be patient and tough; one day this pain will be useful to you.
author: Ovid

text: Dimidium facti qui coepit habet: sapere aude. — He who has begun is half done: dare to know.
author: Horace

text: Per aspera ad astra. — Through hardships to the stars.
author: Latin proverb

text: Festina lente. — Make haste slowly.
author: Augustus (via Suetonius)

text: Nulla dies sine linea. — No day without a line.
author: Pliny the Elder, about Apelles

text: Fatti non foste a viver come bruti, ma per seguir virtute e canoscenza.
author: Dante Alighieri (Inferno XXVI)

text: Learning never exhausts the mind.
author: Leonardo da Vinci

text: Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication.
author: Attributed to Leonardo da Vinci

text: I have been impressed with the urgency of doing. Knowing is not enough; we must apply.
author: Leonardo da Vinci

text: Ancora imparo. — I am still learning.
author: Attributed to Michelangelo

text: Sapere aude! Have courage to use your own understanding.
author: Immanuel Kant

text: He who has a why to live for can bear almost any how.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: That which does not kill us makes us stronger.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: I think, therefore I am.
author: René Descartes

text: Divide each difficulty into as many parts as is feasible and necessary to resolve it.
author: René Descartes

text: Genius is eternal patience.
author: Michelangelo (attributed)

text: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.
author: Attributed to Confucius

text: Real knowledge is to know the extent of one's ignorance.
author: Confucius

text: The journey of a thousand miles begins with one step.
author: Lao Tzu

text: Ever tried. Ever failed. No matter. Try again. Fail again. Fail better.
author: Samuel Beckett

text: We must imagine Sisyphus happy.
author: Albert Camus

text: In the midst of winter, I found there was, within me, an invincible summer.
author: Albert Camus

text: Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known.
author: Sharon Begley (often attributed to Carl Sagan)

text: It always seems impossible until it's done.
author: Attributed to Nelson Mandela

text: The secret of getting ahead is getting started.
author: Attributed to Mark Twain

text: I have not failed. I've just found 10,000 ways that won't work.
author: Attributed to Thomas Edison

text: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.
author: Thomas Edison

text: The important thing is not to stop questioning.
author: Albert Einstein

text: It's not that I'm so smart, it's just that I stay with problems longer.
author: Attributed to Albert Einstein

text: Anyone who has never made a mistake has never tried anything new.
author: Attributed to Albert Einstein

text: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
author: Marie Curie

text: Be less curious about people and more curious about ideas.
author: Marie Curie

text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
author: Isaac Newton

text: What I cannot create, I do not understand.
author: Richard Feynman

text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
author: Richard Feynman

text: Study hard what interests you the most in the most undisciplined, irreverent and original manner possible.
author: Richard Feynman

text: Measure what is measurable, and make measurable what is not so.
author: Attributed to Galileo Galilei

text: Eppur si muove.
author: Attributed to Galileo Galilei

text: Mathematics is the language in which God has written the universe.
author: Galileo Galilei (paraphrase)

text: The more I learn, the more I realize how much I don't know.
author: Attributed to Albert Einstein

text: Tell me and I forget. Teach me and I remember. Involve me and I learn.

text: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.

text: Well done is better than well said.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Whether you think you can, or you think you can't — you're right.
author: Attributed to Henry Ford

text: Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.

text: Nothing will work unless you do.
author: Maya Angelou

text: You may encounter many defeats, but you must not be defeated.
author: Maya Angelou

author: Helen Hayes

text: Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement.
author: Helen Keller

text: Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.
author: Helen Keller

text: I am always doing that which I cannot do, in order that I may learn how to do it.
author: Pablo Picasso

text: Inspiration exists, but it has to find you working.
author: Pablo Picasso

text: Done is better than perfect.
author: Sheryl Sandberg (Facebook poster motto)

text: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.
author: Alan Kay

text: Simple things should be simple, complex things should be possible.
author: Alan Kay

text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
author: Alan Turing

text: Sometimes it is the people no one imagines anything of who do the things that no one can imagine.
author: The Imitation Game (film, about Alan Turing)

text: The most dangerous phrase in the language is: We've always done it this way.

text: A ship in port is safe, but that's not what ships are built for.
author: Grace Hopper

text: That brain of mine is something more than merely mortal, as time will show.
author: Ada Lovelace

text: The more I study, the more insatiable do I feel my genius for it to be.
author: Ada Lovelace

author: Harold Abelson & Gerald Sussman (SICP)

text: Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.

text: The question of whether a computer can think is no more interesting than the question of whether a submarine can swim.
author: Edsger W. Dijkstra

text: Premature optimization is the root of all evil.

text: Science is what we understand well enough to explain to a computer. Art is everything else we do.
author: Donald Knuth

text: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.
author: Linus Torvalds

text: Given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow.
author: Eric S. Raymond (Linus's Law)

text: Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand.

text: If it hurts, do it more often.
author: Martin Fowler

text: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.

text: I'm not a great programmer; I'm just a good programmer with great habits.
author: Kent Beck

text: First, solve the problem. Then, write the code.

text: There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things.
author: Phil Karlton

text: Controlling complexity is the essence of computer programming.
author: Brian Kernighan

text: Debugging is twice as hard as writing the code in the first place.
author: Brian Kernighan

text: Walking on water and developing software from a specification are easy if both are frozen.
author: Edward V. Berard

text: The function of good software is to make the complex appear to be simple.
author: Grady Booch

text: Perfection is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

text: A goal without a plan is just a wish.

text: Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.
author: Attributed to Albert Einstein

text: Stay hungry. Stay foolish.
author: Stewart Brand (Whole Earth Catalog), via Steve Jobs

text: You can't connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backwards.
author: Steve Jobs

text: The people who are crazy enough to think they can change the world are the ones who do.
author: Apple 'Think Different' (1997)

text: If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together.
author: African proverb

text: Fall seven times, stand up eight.
author: Japanese proverb

text: The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago. The second best time is now.
author: Proverb

text: Little by little, one travels far.
author: J. R. R. Tolkien

text: All we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given us.
author: J. R. R. Tolkien

text: It is our choices that show what we truly are, far more than our abilities.

text: Do. Or do not. There is no try.
author: Yoda (The Empire Strikes Back)

text: I am not afraid of storms, for I am learning how to sail my ship.
author: Louisa May Alcott

text: Education is not the filling of a pail, but the lighting of a fire.
author: Attributed to W. B. Yeats (after Plutarch)

text: The mind is not a vessel to be filled, but a fire to be kindled.
author: Plutarch

text: Learning is not attained by chance; it must be sought for with ardor and attended to with diligence.
author: Abigail Adams

text: Live as if you were to die tomorrow. Learn as if you were to live forever.
author: Attributed to Mahatma Gandhi

text: The capacity to learn is a gift; the ability to learn is a skill; the willingness to learn is a choice.
author: Brian Herbert

text: Practice isn't the thing you do once you're good. It's the thing you do that makes you good.
author: Malcolm Gladwell

text: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.

text: Every action you take is a vote for the type of person you wish to become.
author: James Clear

text: Becoming is better than being.
author: Carol Dweck

text: Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most.
author: Attributed to Abraham Lincoln

text: Give me six hours to chop down a tree and I will spend the first four sharpening the axe.
author: Attributed to Abraham Lincoln

text: Our greatest weakness lies in giving up. The most certain way to succeed is always to try just one more time.
author: Attributed to Thomas Edison

text: Hard work beats talent when talent doesn't work hard.
author: Tim Notke

text: Strive not to be a success, but rather to be of value.
author: Albert Einstein

text: I never lose. I either win or learn.
author: Attributed to Nelson Mandela

text: Courage doesn't always roar. Sometimes courage is the quiet voice at the end of the day saying, 'I will try again tomorrow.'
author: Mary Anne Radmacher

text: Chi va piano va sano e va lontano.
author: Italian proverb

text: Volere è potere.
author: Italian proverb

text: Non scholae sed vitae discimus. — We learn not for school, but for life.
author: After Seneca

text: Repetita iuvant. — Repetition helps.
author: Latin proverb

text: Gutta cavat lapidem. — The drop hollows the stone.
author: Ovid

text: Labor omnia vincit. — Work conquers all.
author: Virgil (Georgics)
